output:
# PRD: In-App Substitution Approvals ## 1. Problem When an item is out-of-stock (11.8% of orders, 1.7 items avg in those orders), shoppers substitute on judgement. Customers learn at the door and reject 23% of substitutes. Result: surprise, refunds, waste, bad NPS, and shoppers with no guidance. We will let the shopper propose a substitute in-app, let the customer Approve / Reject / Ask for another before checkout, and apply a safe default on timeout. ## 2. Goals and Success Metrics - **Reduce door surprises:** substitutes rejected/refunded at door/handover from **baseline 23% → <8%** in 60 days. - **Maximize informed consent:** customer response before checkout from **pilot baseline 74% → ≥70%** in prod, without delaying checkout. - **Protect shopper efficiency:** median pick-to-checkout **baseline 34 min, guardrail ≤36 min**; shopper idle per request p95 <60s. - **Protect sales:** % OOS items converted to accepted sub (vs refund) — track, no target cut until V1 data. - **Trust:** sub-related contacts / order stable or down; sub CSAT ≥4.4/5. ## 3. Non-Goals - No ML auto-substitution or personalized ranking in V1; shopper picks from allowed list. - No substitution for age-restricted (alcohol, tobacco) and pharmacy — refund only per licence. - No desktop/web approval, no post-checkout changes, no price-policy rewrite, no offline-mode support. ## 4. User Stories **Customer:** - As a customer, when an item is OOS I get a push + in-app card showing original vs proposed sub, price I will pay, and time left, so I can decide. - As a customer, I can Approve, Reject for refund, or tap “Choose another” to ask shopper for a different option. - As a customer, I know what happens if I miss it, so silence is not a surprise charge. **Shopper:** - As a shopper, I can propose one sub (photo, size, price) and keep picking the rest of the order while waiting, so I’m not idle. - As a shopper, I see Approve / Reject / Another-request + timeout countdown, so I know to pick, refund, or re-propose and still check out on time. ## 5. Functional Requirements **Decision: 180-sec window, Default = REFUND (no substitute).** Justification from pilot (n=1,200): 38% respond by 1 min, 61% by 3 min, 74% by 5 min, 26% never respond before checkout. Median is ~2 min, not <1 min. A 60-sec timeout would force 62% to default. 3 min captures +23pp over 60s (+60% lift). 5 min adds only +13pp for +67% wait. 3 min is the knee of the curve. Default must be Refund because at least 26% never respond even with unlimited time; auto-approve would force unwanted items on >1 in 4 requests, recreating the 23% door-rejection problem. - **FR1:** On OOS, shopper app shows only substitutable items; blocked categories auto-refund with reason. - **FR2:** One active proposal per OOS item. Push + in-app card with original, sub, price-to-pay, timer, actions. - **FR3:** Timer = 180s, visible countdown. Shopper can continue picking (non-blocking). Checkout blocked only until all proposals resolved or timed out. - **FR4:** Actions: Approve / Reject-Refund / Choose another (sends note to shopper, starts one new 180s cycle, max 2 cycles then auto-refund). - **FR5:** Timeout default = Refund. No charge for that line, clearly messaged pre- and post-timeout. - **FR6:** Price display enforces Terms §7.3: customer pays `min(original, sub)`. If sub is pricier, show “You pay $X [original price] — you never pay more.” If cheaper, show lower price. - **FR7:** Audit every event (proposed, approved, rejected, timeout, price shown/charged) for Finance/support. **Stakeholder resolutions:** - *John Stiles (60s + auto-approve):* **Declined.** Data contradicts median claim and 60s strands 62%. Adopted 180s + non-blocking picking + checkout hold to meet “can’t wait” intent without idle. - *Richard Miles (charge sub shelf price if higher):* **Blocked / Escalated to Legal + Product.** Violates published §7.3. V1 ships with price cap. Finance to get weekly upgrade-loss report to motivate a Terms-change proposal with notice/consent if desired. ## 6. Edge Cases - Multiple OOS items: parallel timers; checkout waits for all. - Customer offline / push disabled: in-app inbox + SMS fallback; still times out to refund. - Sub also OOS, or customer asks for blocked item: shopper re-proposes or refunds. - Weight/size differences, allergens: must show size/price-per-unit and flag top-14 allergen mismatch warning. - Customer approves after timeout: treated as no-op, refund stands, apology copy. - Shopper ends pick early: pending proposals collapse to refund. ## 7. Open Questions 1. Legal: process/timeline if we want to amend §7.3 to allow paid upgrades with explicit consent? 2. Assortment: who curates allowed-sub list per store, and quality bar for photos? 3. Tuning: keep 180s globally or 300s for large baskets where async covers wait? 4. Compensation: does shopper wait time count toward batch pay? --- ## Prototype — Customer Approval Screen ```html Basketful - Approve Substitute
BASKETFUL • Order #8421 • FreshMart

Approve a substitute?

🥛 1 item out of stock. Your shopper found a replacement.
⏱ 1:57 remaining to decide
Shopper keeps picking — checkout waits for you.
🥛

Original (out of stock)

Oatly Oat Milk, 64 oz • $4.29

↓ shopper proposes ↓
🌾

Chobani Oat Milk, 52 oz

Plain, shelf price $4.99 • similar, smaller

You pay $4.29 $4.99 • You never pay more than ordered (§7.3)
If you don’t respond: we’ll refund the $4.29 and not add a substitute. No charge, no surprise at the door.
Questions? Terms §7.3 • Refunds in 3–5 days
``` ## Design Rationale Hierarchy puts decision first: urgency timer, original vs proposed contrast, capped price to build trust per §7.3, then large thumb-friendly Approve/Reject with secondary “choose another.” Time bar visualizes 180s without anxiety, and explicit timeout-to-refund copy makes silence safe, reducing door rejections while preserving shopper flow.
